title: --file on a pipe or FIFO bypasses the 8 MiB input cap
detail: The --file path enforces the cap only through fs.stat().size, which is 0 for a pipe, FIFO or /dev/fd/N (for example `--file /dev/stdin` or shell process substitution `--file <(cmd)`). fs.readFile then reads the whole stream with no limit. Confirmed: a 9 MiB body piped through `--file /dev/stdin` is accepted with exit 0, while the same body on plain stdin is refused with 'input is larger than 8 MiB'. So the contract's 'at most 8 MiB' holds for one input method and not for the other. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/design-brief.js.
fix_hint: Refuse anything that is not st.isFile(), or read through a file handle with a bounded read of MAX_BYTES+1 bytes and refuse when that limit is passed.

title: The stdinBytes path and the stdin 8 MiB refusal are never tested
detail: The fake io in the unit test supplies only stdin(), so readInput always takes the io.stdin() fallback. The io.stdinBytes branch, which the real cli.js uses, and its 'input is larger than 8 MiB' refusal are never run by a unit test. The packaged test sends only a small body. The 8 MiB limit is named in the contract, but only the --file side of it is asserted.
fix_hint: Add a fake io with stdinBytes that returns MAX_BYTES+1 bytes and assert the run rejects with /8 MiB/ and code 1, plus one happy-path run through stdinBytes.

title: An empty --file value silently falls back to stdin
detail: `--file ""` passes the parser's value check, but `if (flags.file)` treats '' as absent, so the verb reads stdin instead. Confirmed: `echo '{"kind":"ui"}' | cli.js design-brief questions --file ""` succeeds using stdin. Run on a TTY, the error is 'no input: pass the brief JSON on stdin or --file', which is misleading because --file was passed. The parser also refuses a file whose name starts with '--', and a repeated --file silently keeps the last value.
fix_hint: Test `flags.file !== undefined` and refuse an empty value in run(): `if (!flags.file) throw bad('--file needs a value')`.

title: Packaged test drives only stdin, never --file, through the installed CLI
detail: Each input method should complete the task end to end. The packaged check covers stdin only. The --file path, which depends on the real process.cwd() given by the installed cli.js, is tested only with the unit test's fake io.
fix_hint: In the packaged test, write the body to a temp file in the package dir and assert `design-brief assume --file <f>` exits 0 with the same assumptions as the stdin run.

title: stdin sniff treats a markdown spec as HTML when it has any section/div with an id
detail: The second regex in sniff() matches `<section|div|header|main|body|html ... id=|data-section=` anywhere in the text, including inside fenced code blocks and inline HTML. A markdown spec that shows example markup is checked as HTML, so its headings are ignored. Confirmed: a spec with '## Hero', '## Benefits', '## Final CTA' and a fenced `<section id="faq">` gives found [hero, benefits, final-cta] via --file spec.md but found [faq], missing [hero, ...], cta all false on stdin. The same document gets a wrong result depending only on how it was passed in. Files with an unknown extension (.mdx, none) go through the same sniff.
fix_hint: Sniff HTML only from a leading tag (the first regex), or strip fenced code before the attribute test; add a stdin test with markdown that contains a fenced HTML snippet.

title: 8 MiB stdin cap is not enforced: reads all of stdin, then counts UTF-16 chars instead of bytes
detail: The contract caps input at 8 MiB. The --file path checks st.size in bytes, but the stdin path calls io.stdin() with no { maxBytes }, so cli.js reads the whole stream into memory before any check. It then compares text.length (UTF-16 code units) to MAX_BYTES. Confirmed: 10 MiB of 'é' (5.2M chars) is accepted on stdin, while the same file through --file is rejected. The unit test only uses ASCII 'x', so it cannot catch this.
fix_hint: Use `await io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES })` (as other kit verbs do), reject when buf.length > MAX_BYTES, then decode; add a multibyte over-cap stdin test.

title: Repeated --file silently keeps the last one
detail: `check --file a.md --file b.md` overwrites `file`, so a.md is never checked and nothing reports it. The caller believes two inputs were checked, or does not know which one was.
fix_hint: Throw bad('--file given more than once') when file is already set.

title: Stdin size-cap test uses only single-byte input
detail: The over-cap test feeds 8 MiB + 1 of ASCII 'x', where chars and bytes are the same count, so the test passes even though the stdin cap counts characters, not bytes. A stub io.stdin that ignores maxBytes also passes, so it never checks that the read is bounded.
fix_hint: Add a multibyte case (e.g. 'é'.repeat(4.5 MiB) chars) and have the stub stdin assert it is called with maxBytes.

title: Inline style font-size in markup is missed or mis-skipped
detail:
The header says audit reads a 'CSS/markup file', but the declaration regex only matches font-size after ^, ;, { or whitespace and captures up to ;, } or newline. For

(font-size directly after the quote) nothing is reported: changes [], on_scale 0, skipped []. For style="color:red;font-size:15px"> the value captured is '15px">', so it lands in skipped as 'not a px or rem size' when it should be a change to sm. Confirmed by running auditCss on both strings. Off-scale inline sizes in HTML/JSX templates are silently passed over.
fix_hint: Add quote characters to the lead-in class ([;{\s"']) and stop the value at quotes too ([^;}\n"']*); add a unit test with style="font-size:15px" and style='a:b;font-size:15px'.

title: Line numbering is quadratic; audit takes about a minute on a 1 MB file
detail: lineAt rescans the text from index 0 for every hit, so the cost is O(hits x size). Measured: 50,000 font-size declarations in a 950 KB file took 64.8 s. The verb accepts files up to 8 MiB, where the same density would run for over an hour, which looks like a hang to the caller.
fix_hint: Hits are already sorted by idx: walk them once and count newlines incrementally from the previous hit's index (or precompute newline offsets and binary-search).

title: Stdin is read in full before the 8 MiB cap is checked
detail: io.stdin() is called without { maxBytes }, so cli.js buffers all of stdin into memory before the Buffer.byteLength check runs. The --file path checks st.size first, but piped input does not, so the cap does not bound memory on the stdin path.
fix_hint: Call io.stdin({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES }) so the reader stops once it passes the cap; the existing byteLength check then rejects it.

title: Tailwind text-[length:15px] font sizes are dropped silently
detail: In Tailwind, text-[length:<value>] is the explicit font-size form of an arbitrary text class. The code treats anything that is not a bare px/rem/var/calc/% as a colour class and continues, so text-[length:15px] gets no change, no on_scale count and no skipped entry. The comment wrongly calls these 'not sizes'.
fix_hint: Strip a leading 'length:' prefix from the arbitrary value before the px/rem test, and add a test for it.

title: --file "" silently falls back to stdin
detail: parse accepts an empty string as the value of --file, and the truthiness check `if (flags.file)` then reads stdin instead of failing. From a script that passes an empty variable, this audits whatever is on stdin, or gets 'no input' with a misleading message.
fix_hint: Test flags.file !== undefined, and reject an empty --file value in parse with KitExit 1.

title: --file is not checked to be a regular file and is read unbounded
detail: run() calls fs.stat then fs.readFile with no isFile() check. A FIFO, device or /dev/stdin reports size 0, passes the 8 MiB check, and readFile then reads the stream with no limit (it can hang on an open pipe or pull far more than 8 MiB into memory). The stat/readFile pair is also a TOCTOU: the file can grow after the stat. The Input reading rule in rules.md requires fs.stat(...).isFile() (else exit 1 naming the path) and a bounded read of at most 8 MiB + 1 bytes. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/motion-plan.js.
fix_hint: After stat, throw KitExit 1 when !st.isFile(); read through a file handle with a buffer of MAX_BYTES + 1 and refuse when more than MAX_BYTES bytes come back. Apply to both copies.

title: stdin is read whole through io.stdin(), not the capped io.stdinBytes
detail: The verb calls io.stdin() and only checks Buffer.byteLength after the whole stream is in memory, so the 8 MiB cap does not bound the read. cli.js already passes io.stdinBytes, and rules.md says stdin is read with io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX + 1 }) with the cap counted in bytes.
fix_hint: Read with io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES + 1 }), refuse when the result is over MAX_BYTES bytes, then decode as UTF-8. Apply to both copies.

title: --file "" silently falls back to stdin, and a repeated --file is accepted
detail: With `--file ""`, the value '' passes the value check (it does not start with --), file becomes '', and `if (file)` is false, so the verb reads stdin instead of refusing. A second --file silently replaces the first. rules.md says an empty flag value and a repeated flag are refused with exit 1. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/motion-plan.js.
fix_hint: In the arg loop, throw KitExit 1 when file !== undefined (repeated) or when the value is ''; then test file !== undefined instead of truthiness.

title: Input-reading tests miss what the rule names
detail: The unit tests drive io.stdin, not stdinBytes. The over-cap case is ASCII only, with no multibyte text, so the bytes-versus-length requirement is never exercised. Nothing covers a FIFO or directory --file, an empty --file value or a repeated --file. The packaged test (test/kit-context-split-showcase-or-website-packaged.test.js) sends every input on stdin and never runs --file through the installed CLI, which rules.md requires.
fix_hint: Give the io helper a stdinBytes, and add an over-cap multibyte case, refusal cases for a directory or /dev/stdin, `--file ""` and a repeated --file, plus one packaged run with --file on a temp file.

title: emit has no stdin input path; tests never drive stdin
detail: Shared conventions say input comes from a file or stdin, and the Input reading rule says stdin is read with io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX + 1 }) with the cap counted in bytes. run() only accepts --text-file and ignores io.stdin/io.stdinBytes, so `... | cli.js word-reveal emit` exits 1. The rule also requires unit tests that drive stdinBytes (an over-cap multibyte input and a happy path) and a packaged test that drives both stdin and --file. None of these tests exist (the unit io stub even passes a stdin that is never used).
fix_hint: When --text-file is absent and stdin is not a TTY, read io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES + 1 }), refuse more than MAX_BYTES bytes with exit 1, and decode as UTF-8. Add the unit tests for stdinBytes and the packaged stdin and --file cases.

title: File read is size-checked by stat, not bounded
detail: readFileCapped checks st.size and then calls fs.readFile on the whole file. The rule requires a bounded read of at most 8 MiB + 1 bytes. A file that grows between the stat and the read, or a regular file that reports size 0 but has content (for example under /proc), is read in full with no cap. That holds for both emit --text-file and lint --file.
fix_hint: Open the path, fstat the handle (isFile), read at most MAX_BYTES + 1 bytes into a buffer, and exit 1 if more than MAX_BYTES bytes came back.

title: Repeated flags are silently last-wins; an empty --text-file gives a misleading message
detail: parse() does flags[k] = rest[++i] with no duplicate check. `emit --text-file a.txt --text-file b.txt` emits b's text, and `--muted 0.3 --muted 0.9` uses 0.9. Both were confirmed by running them. The Input reading rule says a repeated flag is refused with exit 1. `--text-file ""` resolves to the cwd and fails with '<cwd> is not a regular file' instead of naming the empty value. A flag value that starts with -- (for example `--text-file --muted`) is also taken as the value.
fix_hint: In parse(), throw bad(`${a} given twice`) if k is already in flags. Refuse an empty value, or one that starts with --, with a message that names the flag.

title: Screen readers may announce the tagline as word fragments
detail:
The fragment is a bare

holding one per word, with no accessible-name strategy. Some screen readers, notably VoiceOver on iOS and Safari, treat each inline span as its own swipe stop, so the sentence is read one word at a time. Nothing gives assistive technology the whole sentence as one unit, and no test checks for it. Putting aria-label on the

is not a reliable fix, because ARIA prohibits naming the generic or paragraph role.
fix_hint: Emit the full escaped sentence once in a visually-hidden span (sr-only CSS), and wrap the word spans in an aria-hidden="true" span. Add a test asserting both.

title: Words stay at muted opacity forever when the script never runs or the block is skipped
detail: The muted opacity is applied by plain CSS (.wr-w{opacity:0.25}), regardless of JavaScript. If the inline script is blocked (CSP without unsafe-inline, JS off, a sanitizer that strips <script>), the tagline is stuck at 25% opacity, which is far below text-contrast minimums. The observer callback (line 86) also reveals only on isIntersecting. If the page loads already scrolled past the block (scroll restore, or an anchor link below it), the block is above the root box and never intersects, so it stays dim until the user scrolls back up.
fix_hint:
Apply the muted state only under a class the script adds (for example, the script sets .wr-js on the

, and the CSS rule becomes .wr-js .wr-w{opacity:muted}). In the callback, also reveal when entry.boundingClientRect.top < entry.rootBounds.top, meaning the block has already been passed.

title: Lint treats any mention of 'throttle' or 'rAF' as throttled
detail: THROTTLE_RE is tested against the raw handler text, comments and strings included. A handler with a comment like `// TODO throttle this`, or a call to an unrelated function named debounceLog, is passed as throttled. The result is a silent false negative for exactly the case the lint exists to catch.
fix_hint: Strip comments and string literals from the handler before testing, and match call sites only, for example /\b(requestAnimationFrame|rAF|throttle|debounce)\s*\(/.

title: Non-breaking spaces are split into ordinary breaking spaces
detail: split(/\s+/) also matches U+00A0. A tagline written with an intentional non-breaking space (for example '10 km' or 'Mr. Smith') is emitted as separate spans joined by a normal space, so the author's no-wrap intent is lost at large font sizes.
fix_hint: Split on /[ \t\r\n\f\v]+/ (ASCII whitespace) so that U+00A0 stays inside a word.

title: Same text gives a different result on stdin than via --file when it opens with an HTML block or a comment
detail:
--file takes its type from the extension (line 220), but stdin uses sniff(), which looks only at the first tag. So the result still depends on how the input arrived, which breaks the rules.md 'Input reading' rule. I confirmed both directions. (1) A markdown spec that starts with a common banner, '
' followed by ## Hero / ## Benefits / ## Final CTA: via --file s.md, found is [hero, benefits, final-cta] and mirrors is true. On stdin it is read as HTML, found is [] and every must section is missing. (2) An HTML page that starts with a comment ('' before ), or with ,
,
and so on: via --file p.html, found is [hero, final-cta]. On stdin it is read as markdown and found is []. Either way a real page gets a wrong 'missing everything' result. No test covers this.
fix_hint: Pick the type from the text alone on both paths: skip leading comments and whitespace, and treat the text as HTML only when it has <!doctype>/<html> or contains no markdown heading outside fenced code. Use the same rule for --file too, or add a --format flag. Add a stdin == --file test for a .md that starts with <div> and for a .html that starts with a comment.

title: Quadratic regex scan on malformed HTML: inputs well under the 8 MiB cap can hang
detail: TAG's attribute part ((?:[^>"']|...)*) can run past '<', so every '<' that has no later '>' scans to the end of the input and then backtracks. htmlLabels (line 145) does the same for each <a>/<button> that is never closed: its lazy [\s\S]*? runs to the end of the body. Measured: '<div id="hero">' + '<a'.repeat(20000) (40 KB) takes 3.5 s, and doubling the input roughly quadruples the time. In the hero body, 20000 unclosed '<a href=x>' take 1.7 s. At the advertised 8 MiB cap, that kind of malformed or truncated input runs for hours instead of finishing or exiting 1, so the byte cap does not bound the work.
fix_hint: Exclude '<' from the unquoted attribute class (e.g. [^<>"']), so a scan stops at the next tag, and bound the label scan per tag (e.g. stop at the next '<a'/'<button' or a section boundary). Add a timing test with a large run of unclosed tags.

title: Regular-file check runs on the path before open, so a swapped-in FIFO can still hang the read
detail: readInput calls fs.stat(file), checks isFile(), and only then calls fs.open(file, 'r') on the same path. If the path is replaced by a FIFO between the two calls (a rename or symlink swap), open(2) blocks until a writer appears and the verb hangs. The window is narrow, so this is low. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/design-brief.js.
fix_hint: Open first with O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK, then run fh.stat() on the handle and refuse when !isFile().

title: The JSON parse error drops the parser's reason and does not say where the input came from
detail: catch { throw bad('input is not valid JSON') } throws away the SyntaxError message, which gives the position, and does not name the --file path or say stdin.
fix_hint: Include the source (file path or stdin) and e.message in the error.

title: Only one refusal checks that its message names the field
detail: The contract says unknown keys and wrong types are refused with a message naming the field. Only answers.audience is checked for that; the unknown top-level key, the unknown answers key, the bad kind and the list-item refusals are checked for exit code 1 only.
fix_hint: Assert the message names the field for each refusal case.

title: Format sniffing depends on how the input arrived (file vs stdin)
detail:
Input reading rule: --file x.md and the same text on stdin must give the same result. Here the format comes from the extension for --file, but stdin is guessed from a short list of leading tags. Two cases checked: (1) a README that opens with '
' and then has '# Get Started With Our Product' gets the title-case finding as --file x.md, but on stdin it goes into HTML mode, markdown headings are skipped (headings() only reads them when !isHtml), and the finding is lost. (2) HTML that opens with '

' on stdin is treated as plain text, so style="width:100%" is flagged as a round figure and the

Title Case heading is missed. As a .html file the same text gives [hype, title-case]; on stdin it gives [hype, round-figure]. The same split happens for JSON at line 233 (sniffed only when there is no extension).
fix_hint: Decide the format from the text alone, or from an explicit --format flag, the same way for both inputs. Also read markdown headings even when HTML tags are present. Add a test that lints the same text through --file and stdin and gets the same findings.

title: stdin and --file reads are not bounded; the cap is checked only after the whole input is in memory
detail: io.stdin() is called with no maxBytes, so cli.js readStdinBytes reads until EOF (limit Infinity). Only then does Buffer.byteLength check 8 MiB, so a large or endless pipe uses unbounded memory or hangs. The rule requires io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX + 1 }). The --file path (line 260) checks with stat and then calls fs.readFile with no limit, so a file that grows after the stat is read in full. The unit test drives a fake io.stdin with a string, so the rule's required stdinBytes tests (a multibyte over-cap case and a happy path) are missing.
fix_hint: Read stdin with io.stdinBytes({ maxBytes: MAX_BYTES + 1 }), check buf.length, then decode. Read the file through a handle with a bounded read of MAX_BYTES + 1. Add unit tests through stdinBytes, including multibyte text over the cap.

title: --file "" silently falls back to stdin; a repeated flag silently wins last
detail: parse() only refuses an undefined value or a value starting with '--'. With --file '', flags.file is '', which is falsy, so run() reads stdin instead. With piped input it lints stdin and reports file:null, exit 0 (checked: run(['lint','--file',''], stdin 'Lorem ipsum') returns 1 finding). A repeated --file or --rules quietly overwrites the earlier value. The Input reading rule says both must exit 1.
fix_hint: In parse(), refuse v === '' and refuse a flag already in flags with KitExit(..., 1). Add tests for both.

title: JSON finding lines are wrong for strings with \n or other escapes
detail: The line is computed as base + f.line - 1, where f.line counts real newlines in the decoded string. In the raw JSON those newlines are '\n' escapes on one line, so the line is pushed past the string. Checked: a lorem in the third segment of the string on line 2 is reported at line 4. Line 195 also searches for JSON.stringify(v) in the raw text, so a string written with different escapes (for example \u00e9 or \/) is not found and its findings fall back to line 1. Body copy stored in JSON often has \n and escapes.
fix_hint: Report the line where the string starts (base) for every finding in it, or map offsets through the raw escaped text. Find the string's position from the parse position instead of re-stringifying. Add a test with a multi-line string and a \u escape.

title: round-figure flags status codes and ordinary counts in realistic copy
detail: Every multiple of 100 that is 100 or more is flagged, with no context check. 'Error 500: server down. Please retry.' and 'Returns 200 OK' each give a round-figure finding, and so do normal pricing and plan copy like '$300 a month for up to 500 seats' and '1,200 reviewers'. This matches the contract's wording but cries wolf on real marketing and error copy, so people will learn to ignore the advisory output.
fix_hint: Skip numbers right after words like error, status, HTTP or code, and numbers followed by OK, so 'Error 500' and '200 OK' are not flagged. Consider flagging only 1,000 or more, or only numbers next to claim words such as users, customers or teams, when they are not prices.

title: lineOf rescans the input from offset 0 for every finding, so lint time is quadratic
detail: add() at line 117 calls lineOf(src, idx), which counts newlines from 0 to idx on every call, so a run costs input length times finding count. Measured with lint(): a 1.9 MB markdown doc with 4,000 round-figure findings (one '$1,000 for 500 seats' line every 10 lines) took 11.1 s, and 1 MB with 55,000 findings ('We use 100% of it.' repeated) took 80 s. Both are well under the 8 MiB cap the verb accepts, so a large spec or a generated sample page under the cap can make the advisory linter look hung.
fix_hint: Build the newline offsets once per lintText call (an array of indices of '\n') and binary-search it in add(), or sort findings by index and walk forward once. Add a timing-bounded test, for example a 2 MB input with a few thousand findings finishing in under 1 s.

title: vague-error counts words that describe the failure as a next step
detail: NEXT_STEP matches action words anywhere in the rest of the line and the next line, including words that only say what failed. Checked with lint(..., {rules:['vague-error']}): 'Something went wrong while we tried to add your card.' gives 0 findings ('add'), 'Something went wrong with your sign in.' gives 0 ('sign in'), and 'An error occurred. Please' gives 0 ('please'). These are exactly the vague error messages with no next step that the contract says to flag, and they are common in real failure copy, so the rule misses them without any notice.
fix_hint: Look for a next step only after the end of the vague phrase's sentence (text after the first . ! or ?, or on the next line), and match imperative phrases such as 'try again', 'check your', 'contact' or 'refresh' instead of bare words like add, use, see and please. Add the three strings above as negative cases in the vague-error test.

title: Unclosed <script, <style, <!-- or <a tags make the HTML regexes quadratic
detail: htmlToText's /<(script|style)\b[\s\S]*?<\/\1\s*>/ and //, and the heading regex at line 94, scan to the end of the input for every opener that has no closer. Measured: 'x' plus '
fix_hint: Find each closer with indexOf from the opener, and when it is missing blank to the end of the input once and stop, instead of retrying the regex at every later opener.

title: Deeply nested JSON overflows the recursive walker and fails with an unclear error
detail: JSON.parse accepts deep nesting, but lintJson's value() recurses once per level. '['.repeat(20000) + ']'.repeat(20000) (40 KB, which detectFormat sniffs as JSON) throws RangeError 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'. It is not a KitExit, so cli.js prints 'kit: Maximum call stack size exceeded' and exits 1. The message does not name the input or say what was wrong with it.
fix_hint: Walk with an explicit stack, or catch RangeError in lint() and throw bad('input JSON is nested too deeply'). Add a test for that case.

title: Box blur erases period-(2r+1) content: a visibly different frame passes as identical
detail: The PSNR is computed only on box-blurred images, and a box filter of window 2r+1 has exact spectral zeros. Any difference whose pattern has period 2r+1 along a row (e.g. +d,-2d,+d repeating, which also survives the clamped edges when the width is a multiple of 3) blurs to zero. Confirmed: a 6x6 uniform gray 100 ref against vertical stripes 140/20/140 (raw PSNR about 10 dB) gives {psnr:null, identical:true, pass:true} at the default --blur 1. Regions use the same blurred buffers, so they do not catch it either. For a blocking judge this is a wrong pass on 1px periodic content such as dotted borders, hatching or dithering, and identical:true (line 269) claims the frames are equal when they are not.
fix_hint: Use a gaussian blur, which has no spectral zeros (the contract allows box or gaussian), or apply a floor from the unblurred PSNR. Compute identical from the raw composited pixels, not from the blurred MSE. Add a test with a period-3 stripe pattern that must fail.

title: A --diff-out write error replaces a failing verdict with a non-blocking exit 1
detail: run() computes the verdict (exit:2 on a failure) and then calls writeAtomic. If the diff cannot be written (parent directory missing, read-only, the path is a directory or a symlink), writeAtomic throws KitExit 1 and the verdict is lost. exit-codes classes 1 as 'usage', which never blocks, so a failing frame passes the UI gate. Confirmed: --ref solid(100) --actual solid(180) --diff-out nodir/d.png throws code 1 (ENOENT) instead of returning exit 2. A CI step that writes the diff into an artifacts/ folder nobody created is a normal setup, and every failing frame then gets through.
fix_hint: Check that the --diff-out target can be written before comparing, or catch the write error once the verdict is known, keep exit 2 and report the write problem in the result (e.g. diff_out_error). Add a test: a failing compare with an unwritable --diff-out still gives exit 2.

title: 50-megapixel cap lets a 190 KB PNG pair use 4.5 GB RAM and take 68 s
detail: MAX_PIXELS allows 50M pixels, and the working set grows to many times the pixel count: raw, unfiltered and RGBA byte buffers for each image, plus a Float32 composite, blur tmp and blur out for each image, plus a second blur pair for the structural retry, plus another composite pair in diffPng. Measured: two 7000x7000 RGBA PNGs of 190 KB each, with one failing region, reached 4542 MB max RSS and took 67.8 s. inflateSync's maxOutputLength bounds only the inflate, not what follows. On a smaller CI runner this ends in an OOM kill, which is infrastructure (non-blocking), so a hostile or accidental huge actual frame also gets past the judge.
fix_hint: Lower MAX_PIXELS to a size that fits real UI frames (e.g. 16 MP), or budget memory from width*height*bytes per stage. Free the raw and out buffers early, reuse blur buffers, and blur only the failing regions' bounding boxes for the retry.

title: --diff-out can overwrite the --ref or --actual input
detail: writeAtomic refuses symlinks and non-regular files, but it does not check that the target differs from the input files. Confirmed: --ref ref2.png --actual off.png --diff-out ref2.png replaces the reference frame with the amplified diff image. Every later run then compares against a diff picture, so the reference is lost (data loss) and later verdicts are wrong.
fix_hint: Resolve --diff-out and refuse it with exit 1 when it equals the resolved --ref or --actual (also compare dev+ino when the file exists).

title: Unknown critical chunks and out-of-order PLTE/tRNS are accepted silently
detail: The chunk loop ignores every type it does not know, including critical ones (uppercase first letter), which the PNG spec says a decoder must reject. It also accepts PLTE or tRNS after IDAT. The decoder can therefore score a file it cannot actually interpret, instead of refusing it with a clear message.
fix_hint: Refuse an unknown chunk whose type byte 0 is uppercase (bit 5 clear), and refuse PLTE or tRNS after the first IDAT, with KitExit 1.

title: readBounded checks the path with stat, then opens it (TOCTOU)
detail: isFile() is checked on the path before fs.open, so a path swapped to a FIFO between the two calls blocks open/read forever, which is the hang the Input reading rule's FIFO refusal is meant to prevent.
fix_hint: Open first with O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK (and O_NOFOLLOW if wanted), then fh.stat() and check isFile() on the open handle.

title: Test named for FIFO refusal never uses a FIFO or /dev/stdin
detail: 'input rules: directories, FIFOs-like non-regular files...' only tests a directory. The rule names FIFO, device and /dev/stdin refusal specifically, so a regression in that path would not be caught.
fix_hint: Add a case for --ref /dev/stdin (or a mkfifo FIFO on POSIX) that must exit 1 with 'not a regular file' and must not hang.

title: Regression description now misleads for fidelity
detail: Once fidelity is in PRODUCT_JUDGES, classify/describe for a fidelity exit 2 returns the generic regression text: 'Pass --result ... for the hit count, the first unscanned paths with reasons and a remedy'. None of that applies to a PSNR verdict, and passing --result adds nothing, so the text sends the reader after information that does not exist.
fix_hint: Make the generic text verb-neutral, or add a fidelity description that reads frame psnr/target and the failing region ids from --result.

title: effects_even with an uneven overhang skips overhang-offset, against the contract
detail: The contract's decision table reads 'clipped_by_parent or effects_even -> overhang-offset'. The code adds an extra condition, effects_even && isEven(ov), so a layer that sets effects_even and has an uneven render_bounds overhang falls through to the later rules. Checked by hand: bounds {10,10,40,20}, render_bounds {6,8,50,26}, effects_even true, no stroke_geometry. The contract gives overhang-offset at 6,8 50x26. The code returns rule 'bounds' at 10,10 40x20 and adds a warning saying 'no clipping or even effects', which is false because effects_even was set. The same change is in .claude/helpers/kit/layer-place.js:129 and the header comment, and the test at test/kit-layer-export-placement-math.test.js:83 locks the deviation in.
fix_hint: Use the contract's condition (rb && (clipped_by_parent || effects_even)) or get the contract changed on purpose. Either way, make the fallback warning say which flag was set and why the rule did not apply.

title: Exact-cap test name says it fails as JSON, but it asserts 'no input'
detail: The test 'accepts input of exactly the cap in bytes (then fails as JSON, not as size)' sends 8 MiB of spaces, so it checks the empty-input branch (/no input/), not the JSON-parse branch its name describes. It still shows the size check passed, but the name misleads the reader.
fix_hint: Pad a valid JSON body with whitespace up to exactly MAX_INPUT_BYTES and assert it succeeds, or rename the test to match what it asserts.

title: --file temp dir is created at describe time and removed only by the last test
detail: mkdtempSync runs when the describe block loads, and rmSync is the last line of the final it(). If an earlier assertion in that test fails, or the tests are filtered by name, the temp dir is never removed. That breaks the convention of a fresh temp dir per run, removed afterwards.
fix_hint: Create the dir in before() and remove it in after() inside the --file describe block.

title: --file /dev/stdin is accepted when stdin is redirected from a regular file
detail: rules.md says a FIFO, device or /dev/stdin given to --file is refused with exit 1. The code only checks fs.stat(p).isFile(), and stat follows /dev/stdin -> /proc/self/fd/0. When stdin is redirected from a regular file, that check passes. Confirmed: `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js motion-plan --file /dev/stdin < plan.json` exits 0 and prints a plan. The same holds for /dev/fd/N and /proc/self/fd/N. The unit test '--file refuses /dev/stdin' passes only because the test runner's stdin happens not to be a regular file, so it depends on the environment: run it under `node --test ... < somefile` and it would fail or misbehave. Same code in .claude/helpers/kit/motion-plan.js.
fix_hint: Before the stat, refuse a path whose fs.realpath (or the resolved path itself) is /dev/stdin, /dev/fd/* or /proc/*/fd/*, or simply refuse any path under /dev or /proc, with KitExit 1 naming it. Apply to both copies, and have the test pass a regular file as stdin so it does not depend on the environment.

title: isFile check runs on the path before open, not on the opened handle
detail: run() calls fs.stat(p) and then readBounded calls fs.open(p, 'r') on the same path. If the path is replaced by a FIFO in between, fs.open with no writer blocks forever, and the regular-file check never sees it. It is a narrow race, but it is the hang the rule is meant to prevent. Same code in .claude/helpers/kit/motion-plan.js.
fix_hint: Open with fs.constants.O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK, then run fh.stat() on the open handle and refuse unless isFile(); keep the bounded read. Apply to both copies.
